feed.title: Off the Roll: what's new
feed.subtitle: What has been added, by date: states, constituency and district pages, sources and tables on the Special Intensive Revision of the electoral rolls.

entry.title: 27 October 2026: 2 additions
entry.summary: Protests and disputes: the Election Commission's affidavit in the Supreme Court, which says all three SIR orders were unanimous, that a suggestion or query by one Commissioner on a file is not a decision of the Commission, and that Form 6 was not amended although the declaration shown online with it
entry.content:
• Protests and disputes: the Election Commission's affidavit in the Supreme Court, which says all three SIR orders were unanimous, that a suggestion or query by one Commissioner on a file is not a decision of the Commission, and that Form 6 was not amended although the declaration shown online with it could be read as an amendment. The Commission's press note of 26 September had said the declaration attached to Form 6 for the SIR was upheld by the Supreme Court
  • Protests and disputes: the Commission told the Supreme Court that the West Bengal appeals against the inclusion of electors were filed by officers of the state Chief Electoral Officer and were not placed before the Commission

entry.title: 26 October 2026: 15 additions
entry.summary: Protests and disputes: the Supreme Court issued notice to the Election Commission on the plea against deletions in Maharashtra, declined to extend the claims period or stop the final roll, and will hear it on 5 November. The Chief Justice orally assured that no elector deleted in the revision would
entry.content:
• Protests and disputes: the Supreme Court issued notice to the Election Commission on the plea against deletions in Maharashtra, declined to extend the claims period or stop the final roll, and will hear it on 5 November. The Chief Justice orally assured that no elector deleted in the revision would be prosecuted for applying again through Form 6
  • Protests and disputes: Uttar Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer ordered a re-check of every Form 6, 7 and 8 entered by computer assistants since 10 April, and Karnataka, where The Hindu found 61,059 Form 7 applications filed by registration officers themselves with no reason given
  • Protests and disputes: Uttar Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer replied on X to Sanjay Singh of the Aam Aadmi Party over a voter slip that read “Ram ne Yadav ko Maara”, accepting that an error was made and saying computers and software are not casteist
  • Protests and disputes: Maharashtra, where lists of electors with pending notices had been published for 39 of 288 Assembly constituencies by 24 October, two days before the deadline the Chief Electoral Officer set for all of them
  • Further reading and viewing: The Hindu on Karnataka's Form 7 applications, The Indian Express on the last day of Delhi's camps, The Wire on Uttar Pradesh seats set against their 2022 margins, and Frontline on the Commission's response to the revision
  • Further reading and viewing: The Wire on Jawhar Sircar's nine questions to West Bengal's Chief Electoral Officer
  • Events: the INDIA bloc's mock impeachment of the Chief Election Commissioner in Delhi on 30 October, and BJP marches in Hyderabad on 2 November, Karnal on 5 November and Malappuram on 6 November
  • Events: marches in Dhurpur on 26 October and H. D. Kote on 27 October, and a protest in Yadgir on 28 October
  • Notices: Telangana, where hearings on 91,09,213 notices had been held and 39,242 electors found ineligible for the final roll by 24 October
  • Corrections: Bihar's roll before the revision is now the Commission's count of 7,89,69,844 electors on 24 June 2025, in place of the rounded 7.89 crore, which moves the all-India totals slightly
  • Further reading and viewing: a new group for parties' accounts, starting with Organiser's piece setting out the BJP's answers to seven claims about the revision
  • New: a feed of What's New for feed readers, and calendar files of every state's draft and final roll and the Supreme Court's dated orders, one for India and one for each state
  • New: compare two to four constituencies of the same state side by side, print a one-page brief of any constituency, and embed the India chart or a state's chart on another site
  • New: an alert by email when a state's final roll is published, for the states still waiting, and a Cite this page box on every page
  • New: an index of every data file with its columns, size and licence, open for other sites to load

entry.title: 25 October 2026: 14 additions
entry.summary: Protests and disputes: Uttar Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer took five booth level officers and a computer assistant off roll work in Azamgarh after one elector's name was found 13 times, and ordered action against the registration officers
entry.content:
• Protests and disputes: Uttar Pradesh's Chief Electoral Officer took five booth level officers and a computer assistant off roll work in Azamgarh after one elector's name was found 13 times, and ordered action against the registration officers
  • Protests and disputes: Newslaundry's investigation in Kichha, Uttarakhand, where 4,390 names on the draft are missing from the final roll and one booth agent filed 5,359 of the 6,884 Form 7 objections accepted, and a Dharavi resident booked for filing 24 Form 7 objections in one day
  • Further reading and viewing: the Newslaundry investigation, and BBC News Hindi on electors entered under two or three EPIC numbers in Bareilly and Pilibhit Sadar
  • Events: an INDIA bloc march in Agartala on 30 October, a BJP campaign in Dakshina Kannada from 25 October to 30 November, and gatherings in Kakkanad on 28 October and Agra on 30 October
  • Notices: Haryana, where about 2.10 lakh electors sent notices were found ineligible by 24 October
  • Protests and disputes: clerical errors and more than 100 duplicate names found on the roll of the Allahabad-Jhansi graduates' constituency before its Legislative Council poll of 23 October, and the BJP's complaint of 4,397 duplicates on the same roll, which was prepared afresh and is separate from the Assembly roll revised in the SIR
  • Further reading and viewing: Dhruv Rathee's interview in Hindi with S.Y. Quraishi, Chief Election Commissioner from 2010 to 2012, on how rolls were kept before the revision, how the Commission now takes its decisions, Form 6, and West Bengal
  • Further reading and viewing: the panel on S.Y. Quraishi now carries five passages from his interview with Dhruv Rathee, on India's adults and the roll, how the Commission takes its decisions, West Bengal's adjudication, the 13 crore, and a separate form in place of Form 6, each set beside the official figures
  • RTI Replies: the Election Commission's reply of 16 October, reported by the Hindustan Times, which withheld the name and version of the software used to find errors in the rolls under Section 8(1)(d), said no new software had been developed or procured for the revision, and treated the questions on automatic flagging and artificial intelligence as clarifications outside the RTI Act
  • ECINET: the same reply, set beside the Commission's answer of 21 July on the West Bengal module, which cited the same section
  • RTI Replies: the reply of 16 October on the software is now read from the application and the reply themselves, filed on 27 July, received on 31 July and answered in 81 days
  • District pages now load only their own state's district circumstances, about 10 KB in place of 227 KB, and the Uttar Pradesh page loads two small counts in place of about 480 KB
  • Reports: the contents list at the top of each report now shows on phones and on wide screens
  • Downloads: the Uttar Pradesh report and slide deck are rebuilt, so the deck's takeaway on winning margins now says the seat counts are an estimate from district figures

entry.title: 24 October 2026: 21 additions
entry.summary: Protests and disputes: the Punjab Assembly's resolution of 23 October asking for an independent inquiry into alleged irregularities in voter lists under the Chief Election Commissioner, the first by an Assembly
entry.content:
• Protests and disputes: the Punjab Assembly's resolution of 23 October asking for an independent inquiry into alleged irregularities in voter lists under the Chief Election Commissioner, the first by an Assembly
  • Protests and disputes: more than 150 people detained at the People's March in Delhi on 23 October, arrests at a sit-in in Chennai on 22 October, and the Left Democratic Front's walkout from the Kerala Chief Electoral Officer's meeting
  • Protests and disputes: Karnataka's Form 7 applications, which rose from 58,475 on 23 September to 2,28,917 by 22 October
  • Further reading and viewing: Surjit S. Bhalla's reply to Jean Drèze and Yogendra Yadav, The Hindu on inclusion applications in Karnataka's most backward districts, and The Indian Express on Delhi's 33 lakh notice cases
  • Further reading and viewing: the panel on Surjit S. Bhalla now includes three passages from his column of 24 October, where he puts the eligible voters left off the nine rolls at about 1 crore, set beside the official figures for the same states
  • Notices: Karnataka's Chief Electoral Officer says hearings for all 43.82 lakh electors sent notices were over by 23 October
  • Protests and disputes: the Supreme Court's remark of 12 October that it had neither approved nor disapproved the new Form 6, the Delhi application on Form 6 now heard on 28 October, the Maharashtra petition listed for 26 October, and a petition of 24 October asking for an expert committee on the Commission's working
  • Protests and disputes: The Wire's follow-up of 24 October finding the Commission appealed against 16,08,175 of the 32,53,401 voters cleared in West Bengal, Jantar Mantar's de-notification, the traders' petition against the protest in Connaught Place, the Karnataka High Court's stay in the Belagavi Form 7 case, and the Maharashtra Chief Electoral Officer's letter on Form 6
  • Further reading and viewing: The Wire's investigation of 24 October into the timing of the Commission's appeals in West Bengal
  • Further reading and viewing: the panels on Rahul Gandhi, Gyanesh Kumar, P. Chidambaram, S.Y. Quraishi and Surjit S. Bhalla now carry the Supreme Court's remark of 12 October and the count of nine states still awaiting a final roll
  • Notices: Delhi's notices decided to 23 October, Telangana's hearings and ineligible electors to 18 October, an Andhra Pradesh hearings count of 29 September, and Meghalaya's figures now cited to the Chief Electoral Officer's own press notes
  • Events: the human chain on Tank Bund in Hyderabad on 24 October, as The Indian Express reported it
  • How the Revision Works: Maharashtra's final roll moved to 16 November and Andhra Pradesh's to 30 October, with the sources for each
  • Constituency pages: the winning-margin sentence now names which fall in the roll it compares and gives its number, the women chart names the roll it compares, and the district chart now draws on 14 constituency pages in Rajasthan and Assam where every seat in the district saw its roll rise
  • Uttar Pradesh: the takeaway on winning margins now says the seat counts are an estimate from district figures
  • West Bengal and Kerala: each district and constituency page now gives the fall in the roll to the roll the 2026 election was held on beside the fall to the draft, so the figure on the state map is on the page it links to
  • Punjab: the fall in the roll is now measured from the roll before to the final roll, 13,60,316, and a note gives the Chief Electoral Officer's count at the draft, 27 names below the count at the end of enumeration
  • Menus: page names now match their titles, in sentence case. Rules is now How the revision was run, Progress is Where the revision stands, Numbers is The SIR in numbers and Comparisons is Reserved seats, final rolls and borders, and the All India menu and section bar follow one order
  • Contents lists at the top of the All India overview, Protests and disputes, How the revision was run, Case studies and Further reading and viewing, and the filters on Protests and disputes moved up under the findings
  • Front page: the state cards now stay in alphabetical order after the featured state, and the page loads less data
  • Wording: sentences across the pages, panels and reading list rewritten as full sentences in plain words, with the five translations updated

entry.title: 23 October 2026: 5 additions
entry.summary: RTI replies: the Cabinet Secretariat's notes on the two Election Commissioners' letters of 29 July about the work allocation order, which it acknowledged and placed on record without acting, holding that the letters came from the Commissioners individually, with the note and both letters as The Wire
entry.content:
• RTI replies: the Cabinet Secretariat's notes on the two Election Commissioners' letters of 29 July about the work allocation order, which it acknowledged and placed on record without acting, holding that the letters came from the Commissioners individually, with the note and both letters as The Wire printed them
  • Protests and disputes: an FIR in Pilibhit against the constituency's two former Electoral Registration Officers and a computer operator, after the Chief Electoral Officer's inquiry found 10,470 approved changes to voters' details with no forms on record
  • Protests and disputes: Delhi's revised report of applications disposed of, which the Chief Electoral Officer's office put up on 22 October after officials said the earlier figures were wrong, now showing 1,07,451 of 4,59,796 inclusion applications disposed of, and two reports on Form 7 objections, one finding a third of Delhi's not listed publicly and one tracing the Commission's change from no limit in West Bengal in January to ten per voter in October
  • Further reading and viewing: The Hindu's report of Karnataka's claims and objections, with 76,176 inclusion applications rejected
  • Events: the People's March to Reclaim Democracy of 23 October now gives the organisers' own map of 58 gatherings in 13 states, with the New Delhi gathering at Gurudwara Bangla Sahib from 1 pm, and five more gatherings from the same map in Hyderabad, Mumbai, Palakkad and Vijayawada between 24 October and 1 November

entry.title: 22 October 2026: 11 additions
entry.summary: Protests and disputes: The Wire's report of 21 October that the Election Commission had appealed against the inclusion of 14,75,887 West Bengal voters whom judicial officers had found eligible, about half of those in the records, and the Uttar Pradesh Congress's allegations about Pilibhit Sadar's ro
entry.content:
• Protests and disputes: The Wire's report of 21 October that the Election Commission had appealed against the inclusion of 14,75,887 West Bengal voters whom judicial officers had found eligible, about half of those in the records, and the Uttar Pradesh Congress's allegations about Pilibhit Sadar's roll
  • Further reading and viewing: The Wire's count of the Commission's appeals in West Bengal by district and seat, and The Hindu's report of 22 October setting the enumeration form beside Form 4 of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960
  • Events: the Uttar Pradesh Congress's press conference of 21 October in Lucknow
  • RTI replies: a new section for the Election Commission's other replies during the revision, with two orders of 12 and 21 October that cite Section 7(9) to decline compiling the information asked for
  • Events: a new page of Jan Sunwais, marches, protests, rallies and press conferences about the revision, by groups and by political parties, coming up and past, each with the announcement or report that gives its date
  • ECINET: a new page that sets every item about the Commission's software in date order, from its announcement in May 2025 to the review of its code
  • Rolls against adults: a new page with two charts, each state's roll against its projected adults before the revision, in the draft and in the final roll, and how much of what the draft lost came back by the final roll
  • Protests and disputes: The Wire's report of 21 October on the review of ECINET's code, which found a VIP marker against some voters on officials' screens and a button to download a list of them, and Millennium Post's report of the Trinamool Congress asking the Commission to explain the West Bengal rule
  • Further reading and viewing: The Wire's report on the review of ECINET's code
  • Further reading and viewing: a panel on Jean Drèze's column of 21 October in The Economic Times, eight quotations set beside the official figures for the same states
  • Further reading and viewing: Jean Drèze's column of 21 October in The Economic Times, which sets the rolls of the major states against their projected adults before the revision, in the draft and in the final lists

entry.title: 20 October 2026: 7 additions
entry.summary: Further reading and viewing: a panel on Surjit S. Bhalla's argument of 17 October that the revision kept about 70 lakh eligible people off the rolls in nine states, set beside the official figures for the rolls and the projected adult population
entry.content:
• Further reading and viewing: a panel on Surjit S. Bhalla's argument of 17 October that the revision kept about 70 lakh eligible people off the rolls in nine states, set beside the official figures for the rolls and the projected adult population
  • Further reading and viewing: a panel on Jean Drèze and Yogendra Yadav's reply of 20 October, which counts more than 7 crore adults missing from the final rolls of the same nine states, set beside the same figures
  • Further reading and viewing: Bhalla's column in The Indian Express (subscription) and his longer post of 17 October, and the reply by Drèze and Yadav
  • Protests and disputes: the Hindustan Times report of 20 October on a review of ECINET's public code, which found a rule that can bar registration officers in West Bengal from the page showing each enumeration form and from the notice-and-hearing dashboard, and no such rule for any other state
  • Further reading and viewing: the same Hindustan Times report
  • Protests and disputes: the Supreme Court's listing on 15 October of a plea about deletions in Maharashtra for 26 October, with the Chief Justice saying the Court would take the states one at a time
  • Notices: Karnataka's count of 16 October, 43.63 lakh hearings held of 43.82 lakh notices

entry.title: 19 October 2026: 10 additions
entry.summary: Left off the roll? What to do: the Delhi High Court's order of 14 October on two electors left off Delhi's roll after they moved house. The Commission's counsel told the Court they could file Form 6, and the Court said their fear of being accused of a false declaration was misplaced
entry.content:
• Left off the roll? What to do: the Delhi High Court's order of 14 October on two electors left off Delhi's roll after they moved house. The Commission's counsel told the Court they could file Form 6, and the Court said their fear of being accused of a false declaration was misplaced
  • Further reading and viewing: the panel on S.Y. Quraishi's post now carries the Delhi High Court's order of 14 October and the Supreme Court petition on the same question, listed for 28 October
  • Further reading and viewing: a panel on P. Chidambaram's post of 16 October about the summary revision, set beside the text of the Commission's letter of 15 October
  • How the revision was run: the Commission's letter of 15 October ordering a special summary revision in the 17 states and union territories where the revision is over, with draft rolls on 12 November 2026 and final rolls on 4 January 2027
  • How the revision was run: two press reports on Delhi, the Chief Electoral Officer's drive of 14 October to find electors left off the draft and the special camps of 18 and 25 October
  • Protests and disputes: the Delhi High Court's order of 14 October on Form 6, and The Wire's report of 17 October that 5,38,320 names were deleted from West Bengal's roll after the draft through Form 7s the Commission's software generated
  • RTI replies: two replies to The Reporters' Collective on whether anyone deleted in the revision was referred to the authority under the Citizenship Act. The Commission transferred the whole application to Bihar, and Bihar's registration officers answered it
  • Further reading and viewing: three more pieces, The Reporters' Collective's report of 16 October on the Commission's records, The Wire's report of 17 October on West Bengal, and the Financial Times of 15 October (subscription)
  • Where the revision stands: Tripura's revision as reported, with house visits from 6 November and a draft roll on 12 December, and Andhra Pradesh's final roll, reported moved to 30 October
  • Every constituency: the front page's finder now also opens the constituencies of Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya and Odisha

entry.summary: About the data: what each count on the site means, from names left off the draft to the fall in the roll, notices and the comparisons with winning margins
entry.content:

  • About the data: Words we use, on why a name left off the draft is kept apart from a name deleted after it, with the sections of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 and the Supreme Court's words
  • Further reading and viewing: panels on what Rahul Gandhi, the Chief Election Commissioner and the Election Commission, Amit Shah, Yogi Adityanath and Mamata Banerjee have said about the revision, 25 quotations each set beside the official figures
  • Further reading and viewing: The Wire's report of 9 October on RTI replies about referring cases to the citizenship authority
  • Further reading and viewing: The Hindu's analysis of 14 October of who was sent notices in Delhi, by religion guessed from names
  • Five more case studies: Bhiwandi East, Anna Nagar, Lucknow, B.B.M.P (South) and Lakhimpur, each the place that lost the largest share of its roll in its own state, with what the records and the reporting say
  • District circumstances from the National Family Health Survey for Andhra Pradesh, Assam, Chhattisgarh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram and Odisha, on every district page and on District factors, which now covers nineteen states
  • Further reading and viewing: 18 more pieces, among them the Commission's letter of 1 October on re-enrolment, the Supreme Court hearing of 5 October, reporting on Odisha, Gujarat and Telangana, and two videos
  • Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Manipur, Meghalaya and Mizoram: every district in a chart and a table on the state page, and for Odisha, Manipur and Meghalaya every constituency set against its winning margin
